stem: Deepak stands at point X facing North. He walks 12 km, turns 90 degrees to his right, walks 5 km, turns 90 degrees to his right again, and walks 12 km. How far is he from X, and in which direction does X lie from his current position?

per_option_rationale.rationale: North 12 -> right (East) 5 -> right (South) 12. Final position: (5, 0). X=(0,0). Deepak is at (5,0). Distance to X = 5 km. X is West of his current position.
Reversing the question asks direction of current position from X (East), not direction of X from current position (West).
Reporting the last leg length (12 km) and only considering the South direction omits the East displacement and the cancellation of North and South legs.
Adding 12 + 5 = 17 km as a total path length and guessing South-West ignores the need to compute net vector displacement.

explanation: Coordinates from X=(0,0): North 12 -> (0,12). Right turn (East) 5 -> (5,12). Right turn (South) 12 -> (5,0). Deepak is at (5,0). X=(0,0) is 5 km to his West.

explanation_sections.punchline: North and South legs cancel; Deepak ends up 5 km East of X, so X is 5 km West of him.
explanation_sections.approach: Apply clues most-certain-first: track coordinates. Two right turns from North: North->East->South. North 12 and South 12 cancel vertically. Net displacement is 5 East, so Deepak is at (5,0). X is in the West direction from there.
explanation_sections.lesson: The question asks for the direction of the START from the END, not the direction of travel. Reverse the displacement vector.
explanation_sections.timing: About 75-90 seconds. The trap is reporting East (direction of current position from start) instead of West (direction of start from current position).
